subject: [PATCH 2/2] cgroup/cpuset: use mems_allowed_seq when checking a policy nodemask

reviews.author: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Identified a potential issue with the comment and code in check_retry_cpuset() and suggested updating them. The patch author disagreed, explaining that they are checking different things.

reviews.author: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Provided a Reviewed-by tag after the patch author addressed some concerns.

2026-10-14.patch_summary: This patch addresses a spurious numa placement miss under certain cpuset/mempolicy combinations by retrying the intersection of mems_allowed and policy nodemask until mems_allowed_seq is stable. The fix involves updating the check in cpuset_nodemask_valid_mems_allowed() to use read_mems_allowed_begin() and read_mems_allowed_retry(). This change ensures that the task's mempolicy and mems_allowed are consistent when checking for valid nodes.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author disagreed that the patch's retry loop is intended to prevent dropping the nodemask on a race, explaining that it ensures stability of nodemask and mems_allowed when compared.
reviews.raw_body:
No I don't think so. We're checking different things.

The loop here makes sure nodemask and mems_allowed are stable when
compared so we don't erroneously drop the nodemask on a race.

The cookie-check in check_retry_cpuset() determines whether the entire
allocation should restart.  It runs after the nodemask would already
have been dropped, so it can't catch this race.

~Gregory

2026-10-15.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's cgroup/cpuset code where a task's mempolicy could be rebound and its mems_allowed changed separately, causing a spurious numa placement miss when checking if a nodemask is valid. The fix involves retrying the intersection of the nodemask with the current task's mems_allowed until mems_allowed_seq is stable. This ensures that the check always sees the updated values, preventing a dropped nodemask and misallocated memory.
